thread:
Evan: quick thought from today's design jam: instead of per-tenant or global anchors, what if we use 'anchor tiles'—group tenants into locality buckets (by region, model_family, traffic profile) and pick an anchor per tile to reduce thrash and KV pressure?
Priya: interesting. tile anchors could reduce noise from tiny tenants while still being more specific than a single global anchor. tradeoffs?
Marta: main tradeoffs: tile granularity vs stability. small tiles approximate per-tenant behavior but cost more state; big tiles reduce state but hide tenant-specific regressions. we need heuristics to form tiles dynamically.
Ben: op impact: fewer anchor lookups if a tile map fits in proxy cache. instead of (tenant->anchor) KV, we do (tile_id->anchor). tile lookup can be a cheap hash + local cache. we still need a way to move tenants between tiles without squirreling anchors.
Jun: how do we map tenants into tiles? static rules are brittle. propose a hybrid: base mapping by region+model_family, then dynamic splits for high-variance tenants (promote to their own tile if they exceed sample/variance thresholds).
Priya: metrics for promotion: sample_rate > X qps && variance_ratio > Y over lookback. demotion if traffic drops & half-life expires. keep tile_metadata: tenant_count, last_rebalance_ts, warmed_cache_bool.
Evan: decision logic for fallback should remain conservative: require a probabilistic signal + deterministic guard. prefer Bayesian posterior P(canary_worse_by_delta | data) >= 0.98 && either error_rate > 1.5% OR p95 > 350ms. also enforce samples >= 250 for tile-level decisions.
observability-bot: ALERT: canary/model-x p95 +26% in eu-west; samples=130; tile=eu-west-ml-medium. link: https://obs.local/d/tiles/canary-x
Ben: below min samples for tile action. do not auto-fallback. instead increase probe fanout for that tile and escalate to oncall if error bursts.
Marta: anchoring lifecycle: tile_anchor table key=(tile_id,model_family)->anchor_version,last_seen_ts,sample_count,confidence,ttl. TTL default 10d. promotion/demotion modifies tile membership and may trigger anchor recompute.
Priya: scoring sketch (pseudocode):
```python
# inputs: latency_delta_norm, error_rate_norm, quality_reg_norm, samples
raw = 0.55*latency_delta_norm + 0.3*error_rate_norm + 0.15*quality_reg_norm
adj = raw * (1 - math.exp(-samples/450)) # penalize small samples
if samples >= 250 and bayes_posterior(canary_worse) >= 0.98 and adj >= 0.72:
    trigger_tile_fallback(tile_id, anchor_priority=[tenant_pinned, tile_anchor, global_anchor, safe_stub])
```
Evan: fallback choreography: rampdown by tile to avoid tenant-level oscillation. default: -25% canary every 45s across tile, but respect tenant overrides (if tenant opted out of auto-fallback). immediate circuit if severity thresholds met (error_rate > 3% AND p95 > 700ms).
Jun: on proxies: implement tile-map cache (LRU) with 60s TTL and background refresh. store mapping in a compact protobuf to minimize RPC cost. background job recomputes tiles every N minutes or on metadata changes.
Ben: storage: shard tile_anchor table by tile_id % 64. keep lightweight records so the table stays small (tile count << tenant count). record anchor_warm_flag so routing can prefer warmed variants.
Marta: observability: emit fallback_event with fields: reason_code, tile_id, posterior, adjusted_score, samples, anchor_used, affected_tenants (sample of tenants). surface in Console and in Optimize for regression triage. also add a tile-level playback endpoint to replay decisions.
Priya: testplan: extend canary-sim harness to support tile topologies: many low-volume tenants, dozens of mid-volume tenants, and a few hot tenants. run sims to tune promotion thresholds and adj scale. add chaos tests where global anchor also degrades.
Evan: rollout plan: start with a read-only tile-map in proxy for a week (no auto-fallback), collect telemetry, run sims, then flip auto-fallback on for non-critical tiles with conservative thresholds. ops: enforce min_samples=250 for auto actions until sims validated.
Jun: one more nit: tenants should be able to request a pinned anchor via API (tenant_pinned). tile logic must respect tenant-level pins and not override them.
Ben: audit: log all tile rebalances and auto-fallbacks to an immutable stream for postmortems and possible replay. expose replay API as Marta suggested.
Marta: i'll start an RFC that includes: tile formation algorithm, promotion/demotion rules, tile-anchor schema, scoring math, proxy cache design, fallback state machine, observability contract. aim to have draft by EOW.
Evan: thanks. @Priya please mock priors and initial weights tomorrow; @Ben prototype tile-cache layout; @Jun sketch tile recompute job; @Marta RFC. Ops: keep auto-fallback disabled until we have sims and min-samples in place.
